task: Write one word in each gap: So I ___ ___ in the queue at the bakery, and this woman suddenly ___ round and hands me her dog. (stand, turn)
explanation shown to learner: In a story told in the present, the background is in the present continuous (*I'm standing in the queue*) and the main events in the present simple (*turns, hands*).
explanation in Latvian: Stāstā tagadnē fons ir Present Continuous (*I'm standing in the queue*), bet *galvenie* notikumi Present Simple (*turns, hands*).

correct answer: So this man is walking into a café and he orders a glass of milk.
wrong options / checks: I was waiting for the bus when suddenly this car stops right in front of me. | We're having dinner when all the lights go out. | In the film, a retired teacher moves to Lisbon and opens a café.
explanation shown to learner: In a joke or a story told in the present, the main events are in the present simple: *So this man walks into a café and orders…* After a past background, a sudden event can be in the present simple (*I was waiting … when suddenly this car stops*): that is correct.
explanation in Latvian: Jokā vai stāstā tagadnē *galvenie* notikumi ir Present Simple: *So this* man *walks into a caf*é *and orders*… Pēc pagātnes fona pēkšņs notikums var būt Present Simple (*I was waiting* … *when suddenly this car stops*): tas ir *pareizi*.

task: Write one word in each gap: And Jones ___ the ball to Taylor, who ___ and scores! (pass, shoot)
explanation shown to learner: In a live commentary, quick actions that are over as you speak are in the present simple: *passes, shoots, scores*. *is passing* would describe a longer action in progress.
explanation in Latvian: Tiešraides komentārā ātras darbības, kas beidzas runāšanas brīdī, ir Present Simple: *passes, shoots, scores*. *is passing* aprakstītu ilgāku darbību, kas vēl notiek.

correct answer: I'm gathering you're looking for a new flat.
wrong options / checks: I hear the bridge will be closed all summer. | Anna tells me you've started running. | It says here the museum is free on Sundays.
explanation shown to learner: To pass on news we have heard or read, we use the present simple: *I gather, I hear, Anna tells me, It says here*. Not *I'm gathering*: *I gather you're looking for a new flat.*
explanation in Latvian: Lai *nodotu* dzirdētu vai izlasītu ziņu, lieto Present Simple: *I gather, I hear, Anna tells me, It says here.* Nevis *I'm gathering*: *I gather you're looking for a new flat.*

correct answer: I'm wondering could you look at my CV before Friday.
wrong options / checks: We're hoping to move in by the end of May. | I was wondering if you were free on Thursday. | I wonder whether you'd mind helping me with this.
explanation shown to learner: After *I'm wondering*, the question becomes *if / whether* + statement order: *I'm wondering whether you could look at my CV.*
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *I'm wondering* jautājums kļūst par *if / whether + apgalvojuma* vārdu secību: *I'm wondering whether you could look at my CV.*

correct answer: I'm wondering whether you could help me with this
explanation shown to learner: A polite request: *I'm wondering whether* + statement order (*you could*), not question order (*could you*).
explanation in Latvian: Pieklājīgs lūgums: *I'm wondering whether + apgalvojuma* vārdu secība (*you could*), nevis jautājuma secība (*could you*).

task: The app ___ to work on my phone. Can you check it? (not / appear)
explanation shown to learner: *appear* = seem is a state: present simple, *doesn't appear to work*. In the meaning *take part* it can be continuous (*She's appearing in a musical*).
explanation in Latvian: *appear* = šķist ir stāvoklis: Present Simple, *doesn't appear to work*. Nozīmē piedalīties, uzstāties var būt Continuous forma (*She's appearing in a musical*).

task: My sister and her husband ___ their first baby in June. (expect)
explanation shown to learner: *be expecting a baby* = she is pregnant, always continuous. In the meaning *think something will happen*, *expect* is simple (*I expect it will rain*).
explanation in Latvian: *be expecting a baby = gaida* bērnu, vienmēr Continuous forma. Nozīmē domāt, ka kaut kas notiks *expect* ir vienkāršajā formā (*I expect it will rain*).

correct answer: I'm promising I'll pay you back on Friday.
wrong options / checks: I suggest we meet at the station. | We regret that the flight has been cancelled. | I'm not suggesting you were careless.
explanation shown to learner: When saying the words is the act itself (promising, suggesting, regretting), use the present simple: *I promise I'll pay you back.* In the negative, *I'm not suggesting* is also correct.
explanation in Latvian: Ja paši vārdi ir darbība (apsolīt, *ieteikt*, izteikt nožēlu), lieto Present Simple: *I promise I'll pay you back.* Noliegumā *pareizi* ir arī *I'm not suggesting.*
